subject: Private upgrade: phased entrainment, health gating, and abort criteria
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@fintechco.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Li <andrew@acme-consulting.com>, ops-support@colossus-cloud.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade — scheduling constraints and rollback expectations

Neha,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. To recap our constraints from the FintechCo side:
- Production is in eu-west-1 and the maintenance window must start after midnight CET on Saturday to avoid trading hours.
- We require a documented preflight and a deterministic rollback path that can return to pinned v1.4.2 within 30 minutes if tests fail.
- Any KV cache drains must not cause request spikes that breach SLAs (we need per-minute rate metrics during drain).

Can you share a high-level plan and the abort/rollback criteria so our ops team signs off? Also loop in any security/compliance artefacts.

Samir
CTO, FintechCo
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Andrew Li <andrew@acme-consulting.com>, ops-support@colossus-cloud.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Private upgrade: phased entrainment, health gating, and abort criteria

Samir — thanks, and good notes. Below is a concise runbook for the weekend upgrade targeting 2026-10-24 (requested maintenance window). Please review; internal teammates, suggest edits.

Summary plan (high level)
- Target: rollout Redwood Private platform upgrade from v1.4.2 -> v1.5.0 (minor changes + security backports).
- Mode: phased entrainment (canary -> staggered cohorts -> full fleet).
- Canary cohort: 2 hosts, 10% traffic, separate KV shard to validate cache behaviour.
- Maintenance window: Saturday 00:30–04:30 CET (UTC+1).

Preflight checklist (attached)
- Validate snapshot of DB & KV, automated smoke tests against pinned v1.4.2 and v1.5.0 images.
- Load test with production-like QPS (replay of 15-minute busiest window) on canary hosts.
- Confirm monitoring hooks for token latency 50p/95p, error-rate, and KV miss-rate.

Health gating and telemetry to accept progression
- Canary acceptance criteria (must be met for 30 minutes):
  - 95th percentile token latency <= 1.25x baseline AND absolute 95p <= 220ms
  - 5xx error rate < 0.05% and not increasing trend
  - KV miss-rate change < +3% absolute; cache rewarm completed
  - No user-facing validation failures in the golden prompt set (automated evals pass)

Staggered cohorts
- If canary passes, promote to rolling cohorts of 20% → 50% → 100% over 30–45 minute windows per cohort. Each cohort requires hold time of 20m for metrics to stabilise.

Abort & rollback criteria (explicit)
- Abort if any of the following within a cohort hold period:
  - 95p token latency rises > 1.5x baseline OR 95p > 350ms
  - Sustained 1-minute spike in 5xx > 0.2%
  - KV miss-rate increases > +10% absolute OR cache warms fail
  - Automated golden-prompt regression: any F1 drop > 4 points
- Rollback plan: switch traffic back to pinned image v1.4.2 via routing policy (DNS/HAProxy weight flip) and trigger automated cache and connection reset. Expected restore-to-steady-state target: 30 minutes.

Operational safeguards
- Circuit-breaker semaphore on control plane to stop all promotions if any NPE/oom/host-cordon occurs.
- Auto-fallback: if dedicated hardware capacity < 2x expected, block rollout.
- Post-mortem triggers: any rollback causes mandatory 48-hour escalation with engineering + CS + customer ops.

Attachments: preflight checklist + rollback playbook. Related runbook live here: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/FintechCo+Private+Upgrade+Runbook

Internal action items
- @dev_patel: confirm KV shard topology for canary and script for cache rewarm.
- @soojin_lee: add bridge-host guard and network ACL verification to the preflight.
- @monica_patel: prepare the customer-facing comms template and Standby rotations for Saturday.

If no major edits, I'll publish this plan to Confluence and share with FintechCo ops by EOD today.

— Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: 20261015-preflight-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), 20261015-rollback-playbook.md (markdown)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: phased entrainment, health gating, and abort criteria

Thanks Neha — this looks solid. A few technical clarifications and recommendations:

- Canary routing: we'll implement traffic steering at the load balancer using weight-based pools rather than DNS to get instant rollback capability. Confirmed: weight flip < 30s to remove traffic.
- KV plan: canary will use independent KV shard + pre-warmed cache snapshot. We'll add a staged TTL ramp to avoid thundering herd.
- Dry-run: propose a dry-run of the exact upgrade workflow in a staging cluster next Wednesday (2026-10-20) with identical orchestration scripts. Recommend we capture packet captures for one canary host to validate network ACL behaviour.
- Circuit breaker: implement a semaphore in the control plane + a 'panic' endpoint accessible to on-call (authenticated) that immediately sets all promotions to zero.

I will update the attached rollback-playbook.md with the specific commands and HAProxy snippets. Also adding a step to validate kernel-level tuning (net.core.somaxconn) preflight — we've seen socket backlog cause slow drain in prior upgrades.

Dev
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick asks from FintechCo ops before we lock dates:

- Provide emergency contact for Saturday night (name + mobile) for your on-call.

We can host a 30-minute run-through with your ops + our on-call on Tue 2026-10-20 at 09:00 CET to walk the rollback steps and go over the dry-run report. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and drop the Confluence link.

Thanks — Monica
